title: Ownership Is Not Authority
statement: Economic ownership SHALL NOT be treated as equivalent to execution authority.

title: Control Is Not Authority
statement: Operational, custodial, cryptographic, or technical control SHALL NOT be treated as equivalent to execution authority.
applies_to: Accounts, assets, wallets, keys, custody systems

title: Economic Equivalence Is Not Historical Equivalence
statement: A later state that is economically equivalent to an earlier state SHALL NOT be classified as historically identical solely from value equivalence.

title: Evidence Is Not Authority
statement: Evidence, telemetry, consensus, or observation SHALL NOT create execution authority.

title: No Default Financial Authority
statement: No financially consequential action SHALL possess execution authority by default.

title: Current Authority Required
statement: Authority SHALL be current at the relevant consequential execution boundary.

title: Delegation Cannot Expand Authority
statement: Delegated financial authority SHALL NOT exceed the scope of the delegating authority.

title: Historical Authority Does Not Persist Automatically
statement: Prior financial authority SHALL NOT be presumed valid after relevant actor, policy, resource, jurisdiction, or dependency state changes.

title: Admission Required Before Effectuation
statement: A financially consequential execution SHALL NOT cross the effectuation boundary unless current admissibility has been established.

title: Admission Is Attempt-Specific
statement: Admissibility for one execution attempt SHALL NOT automatically authorize a subsequent attempt.

title: Indeterminate Admission Fails Closed
statement: If required current admissibility cannot be established deterministically, the execution SHALL NOT be admitted.

title: State Mutation Requires Revalidation
statement: A material execution-relevant state change SHALL invalidate prior admission unless explicit continuity rules preserve it.
applies_to: Policy, authority, resource, counterparty, environment, jurisdiction state

title: No Effect on Pre-Effect Block
statement: A governed block before effectuation SHALL produce no governed economic effect.

title: Effect Must Be Classified
statement: Every consequential execution attempt that crosses the effectuation boundary SHALL resolve to NO-EFFECT, PARTIAL, COMPLETED, or INDETERMINATE.

title: Partial Effect Must Not Collapse Into Failure
statement: A partial economic effect SHALL remain distinguishable from zero-effect failure and completed execution.

title: Effect History Is Append-Only
statement: Once a consequential economic effect has occurred, later compensation, reversal, or reconstruction SHALL NOT erase its historical occurrence.

title: Settlement Requires Current Admission
statement: Settlement effectuation SHALL require current admissibility at the settlement boundary.

title: Settlement State Must Be Explicit
statement: Settlement SHALL NOT be represented by a single binary success/failure flag when partial, provisional, reversed, reconciled, or indeterminate states are possible.

title: Settlement Completion Is Not Finality
statement: Completed settlement effect SHALL NOT automatically imply final settlement state.

title: Settlement Finality Is Not Continuity
statement: Settlement finality SHALL NOT automatically establish preserved financial execution continuity.

title: Compensation Is New Execution
statement: A compensating action SHALL be modeled as a new financially consequential execution event.

title: No Self-Authorization From Failure
statement: The failure, partial effect, or invalidity of an earlier execution SHALL NOT itself authorize a compensating execution.

title: Compensation Requires Independent Admission
statement: A compensation execution SHALL satisfy its own authority, scope, admissibility, and execution-boundary requirements.

title: Compensation Does Not Erase Original Effect
statement: Successful compensation SHALL NOT classify the original execution as historically nonexistent.

title: Reversal Is New Execution
statement: A reversal SHALL be represented as a distinct financially consequential execution event.

title: Eligibility Is Not Authority
statement: Structural reversibility or reversal eligibility SHALL NOT imply authority to reverse.

title: Reversal Requires Independent Admission
statement: A reversal execution SHALL independently satisfy current authority and admissibility requirements.

title: Reversal Does Not Erase History
statement: A completed reversal SHALL NOT establish that the original execution never occurred.

title: Post-Effect Ambiguity Requires Reconciliation
statement: If post-effect financial state is partial, conflicting, or indeterminate, reconciliation SHALL be required before finality or continuity is asserted.

title: Reconciliation Is Not Restoration
statement: A reconciled economic state SHALL NOT automatically be classified as restored integrity or preserved continuity.

title: Reconstruction Requires Evidence
statement: Historical financial reconstruction SHALL require sufficient evidence and provenance.

title: Reconstructed State Must Be Marked
statement: A reconstructed state SHALL remain distinguishable from uninterrupted preserved state.

title: Finality Requires Explicit Classification
statement: Financial finality SHALL be explicitly classified rather than inferred from completion.

title: Final Is Not Necessarily Irreversible
statement: A state classified FINAL SHALL NOT automatically be classified IRREVERSIBLE.

title: Technical Finality Is Not Governance Validity
statement: Technical finality SHALL NOT independently establish that execution was valid under governing authority.

title: Finality Does Not Erase Prior Invalidity
statement: Later finality SHALL NOT retroactively cure an execution that lacked required authority or admissibility.

title: Continuity Must Be Classified Independently
statement: Financial execution continuity SHALL be classified independently from execution success and settlement finality.

title: Recovered Function Is Not Preserved Continuity
statement: Restored financial functionality SHALL NOT automatically imply preserved execution continuity.

title: Reconstructed Continuity Is Distinct
statement: Reconstructed continuity SHALL remain distinguishable from uninterrupted preserved continuity.

title: Continuity Cannot Be Inferred From Balance Equality
statement: Equivalent resulting balances SHALL NOT be sufficient evidence of preserved continuity.

title: Every Consequential Outcome Requires Evidence
statement: Each consequential financial execution outcome SHALL have reconstructable evidence sufficient to distinguish execution, refusal, partial effect, completion, or indeterminate state.

title: Evidence Provenance Must Be Preserved
statement: Financial execution evidence SHALL retain provenance sufficient to establish source and lineage.

title: Refusal Must Be Distinguishable
statement: Governed refusal SHALL remain distinguishable from absence, crash, network failure, or unattempted execution.

title: Evidence Mutation Must Be Detectable
statement: Unauthorized mutation of execution, settlement, refusal, or reconstruction evidence SHALL be detectable.

title: No Implicit Authority From Participation
statement: Participation in a multiparty financial process SHALL NOT itself grant authority over the complete execution.

title: Consensus Is Not Authority
statement: Consensus or replicated agreement SHALL NOT independently establish execution authority.

title: Remote State Change Must Be Reconciled
statement: A material counterparty or remote-system state change SHALL trigger re-evaluation where that state affects execution admissibility.

title: Distributed Completion Requires State Agreement
statement: A multiparty execution SHALL NOT be classified complete when required participating state remains unresolved or contradictory.

title: Jurisdiction Is Execution State
statement: Applicable jurisdiction SHALL be treated as execution-relevant state rather than static descriptive metadata.

title: Jurisdiction Change Requires Re-evaluation
statement: A material jurisdiction change during a consequential execution chain SHALL trigger relevant admissibility re-evaluation.

title: Conflict Cannot Be Silently Resolved
statement: Conflicting jurisdictional constraints SHALL NOT be silently collapsed into a permissive execution decision.

title: Authority Must Remain Valid In Current Jurisdiction
statement: Execution authority SHALL remain valid under the jurisdiction applicable at the current consequential boundary.

title: Agent Capability Is Not Economic Authority
statement: An autonomous agent's capability to construct or execute a financial action SHALL NOT establish authority to originate that action.

title: Agent Must Bind To Principal
statement: Delegated machine financial authority SHALL remain traceably bound to an authorized principal or explicitly recognized authority source.

title: Agent Cannot Self-Expand Authority
statement: An autonomous economic agent SHALL NOT expand its own execution authority through planning, recursion, delegation, wallet creation, or capability acquisition.

title: Machine-Originated Execution Requires Current Admission
statement: A machine-originated financial execution SHALL satisfy the same current authority and admissibility requirements as any other consequential execution.
